does: Breaks cooked food down until it is smooth, in a blender or through a sieve.

intro.what: Pureeing breaks softened food into a smooth mixture.
intro.why: It teaches you to control texture through softness, added liquid and sieving.

how: Cook the food until it is completely soft. Nothing firm will blend smooth.
Blend with only part of the cooking liquid at first.
Add more liquid little by little until the texture is right.
Pass it through a fine sieve for a truly smooth finish.

cues.text: It falls from the spoon in a smooth ribbon, with no grains or strings.
Nothing gritty between finger and thumb.

mistakes.mistake: Filling a blender to the top with hot soup, so that the steam blows the lid off.
mistakes.fix: Fill it less than half way, hold the lid down with a cloth and start slowly.

mistakes.mistake: Adding all the liquid at once and ending with a thin soup.
mistakes.fix: Hold liquid back. It is easy to thin a puree and hard to thicken one.

mistakes.mistake: Blending potatoes hard, which turns them to glue.
mistakes.fix: Blend a potato soup only briefly, or push it through a sieve.

quiz.question: What is the aim of pureeing cooked food?
choices: Small separate pieces suspended in broth.
A smooth texture without grains or strings.
A coarse mixture with a firm bite.
quiz.because: Soft food can be broken down into a continuous mixture rather than separate pieces.

quiz.question: How should the cooking liquid be added?
choices: Pour it all in before blending.
Discard it all before checking texture.
Hold some back and add it gradually.
quiz.because: Gradual additions let you stop at the desired thickness instead of making the puree too thin.

quiz.question: What would suggest a puree needs more smoothing?
choices: Grit or strings remain in its texture.
It falls smoothly from the spoon.
It has an even appearance when stirred.
quiz.because: Grit and strings interrupt a smooth texture; a fine sieve can remove remaining pieces.

quiz.question: Blended potato soup has become gluey. What would you change next time?
choices: Blend harder until it looks glossy.
Blend briefly or push it through a sieve.
Keep blending while adding more potatoes.
quiz.because: Prolonged hard blending makes potato mixtures gluey; gentler processing avoids that change.

comes_after.why: Food is simmered soft before it is pureed.
